craft_notes: Sthāyin: ānanda as delight in variety; bhakti as rati; vyabhicāri joy (harṣa) of seeing variety as one-self. Sanskrit-first: ekātmatā-compound open kept (one-self-nature, unresolved per craft); ramase (WHY-NOT-DELIGHT — question-mood, not command: the verse asks, never orders, per UNC). Abhinavagupta frame: variety (vicitra) unthreatening — the catalogue of feelings IS the universe bodied, no separate nature to fear. Rows: 9 (passion/aversion/pleasure/pain/rise-fall/I-sense/misery — catalogue kept whole; trimming would shrink the variety the verse blesses), 1 (‘contemplating it’ — dhyāna-full delight closes; seeing ends in beholding), 10 (sudden-seeing left as sudden — sahasā kept). Close: ‘full of contemplating it’. Rupture: ‘why not delight’ (seeing turns to delight — the question IS the turn). Rejected: imperative-only delight — killed by UNC (question holds both moods); resolving ekātmatā — killed; trimming feelings — killed: catalogue is the variety. Read aloud: PASS-ion, a-VER-sion, PLEA-sure, PAIN … ARE of NO-sep-ar-ate NA-ture … WHAT-ev-er FORM you SUDD-en-ly SEE — SEE it AS-con-SCIOUS-ness … WHY-not de-LIGHT.

lines: Passion, aversion, pleasure, pain, rise and fall, I-sense, misery and the rest — these states, shining forth, bodied of the universe, are of no separate nature.
Whatever form you suddenly see — see it as consciousness of one self-nature: why not delight, full of contemplating it?
l4.sanskrit_cite: rāgadveṣasukhāsukhodayalayāhaṅkāradainyādayo ye bhāvāḥ pravibhānti viśvavapuṣo bhinnasvabhāvā na te | vyaktiṃ paśyasi yasya yasya sahasā tattattadekātmatāsaṃvidrūpam avekṣya kiṃ na ramase tadbhāvanānirbharaḥ

reads_against.argmap: Why not delight in variety? → Variety is one nature; regard it as consciousness-form, and delight is the only consistent response.
c1_essence: Passions through misery — the whole catalogue of feeling-states, universe-bodied — are not different-natured. Whatever manifestation you suddenly see, regard as one-self-natured consciousness-form: why not delight, contemplation-full? Variety is one nature; the only consistent response to seeing it as consciousness-form is delight.
